article_title: Changes in knowledge, skills, and confidence following a training program for primary care physiotherapists and exercise physiologists in pulmonary rehabilitation: a pre-post study.
citation: Walsh Jessica A., Dale Marita T., McKeough Zoe J., Alison Jennifer A., Dennis Sarah M. (2026). Changes in knowledge, skills, and confidence following a training program for primary care physiotherapists and exercise physiologists in pulmonary rehabilitation: a pre-post study. Primary Health Care Research & Development, 27, e74. https://doi.org/10.1017/S146342362610139X
title: Lung Foundation Australia Pulmonary Rehabilitation Online Training Program
description: A 6–8 hour self-directed online program designed "to increase knowledge and skills of clinicians to deliver evidence-based PR". Modules cover establishing a pulmonary rehabilitation program; the respiratory system and COPD; comprehensive patient assessment; spirometry; assessing exercise capacity; assessing quality of life; exercise training; patient education; and program evaluation and troubleshooting. It embeds an 11-item multiple-choice knowledge test based on a clinical case vignette, with a pre-specified 80% competency threshold. In this study it was combined with a 4-hour practical face-to-face workshop.
requirements: Participants must pass a predefined competency threshold of 80% (9 out of 11) on the embedded knowledge test.
constraints: The spirometry module focuses on interpretation of existing spirometry results rather than performance of spirometry testing itself.
target_learning_goals: Evidence-based pulmonary rehabilitation assessment and delivery
examples: Used as the online component of the training evaluated in this pre-post study, followed by a small-group practical workshop on exercise capacity tests and exercise prescription.
